name: ui-ux
summary: The canvas was correct and said nothing about whether it was good. v1.27 and v1.28 gave the pack a canvas, a front door and an adoption catalog; a review of them found every halt in design-canvas to be a CORRECTNESS check — right tokens, right direction, all states drawn, fully buildable — and not one asking whether the result was worth receiving. /redesign scores against a 15-lens rubric and must beat the old render; /art-direct scores 9 lenses against a scorecard; the canvas scored nothing, drew once and handed over. Three floors close it. (1) THE USABILITY FLOOR, computed and never asserted: text contrast per role (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large), non-text contrast at 3:1 for meaningful UI boundaries — the check people skip and the reason accessible apps still have invisible input fields — target size at 24x24 with the platform convention winning where stricter (44pt iOS, 48dp Android), not-by-colour-alone, and 320px reflow. This is computable HERE and awkward everywhere else precisely because the skill already requires every artboard value to be a literal: in a running app contrast depends on the cascade and must be measured from a render, while on a canvas the numbers sit in the markup. A checkmark where a ratio belongs is now a named failure mode, and NOT RUN is a real printed state, because silence is indistinguishable from success and nobody audits a canvas that appeared to pass. (2) THE QUALITY BAR, borrowing redesign.md's rubric by citation rather than inventing a second design vocabulary, with an explicit split of what a drawing CAN carry (IA, hierarchy, rhythm, cognitive load, states, consistency, locale, modern register, micro-copy; contrast and target size; responsive only where two frames were drawn; beats-the-current-surface only where a baseline exists) from what it CANNOT (motion, which is a build output — a drawing has no hover state; performance; focus order and keyboard behaviour). Deferred lenses are named at every handover so 'approved' cannot quietly come to mean the motion and interaction were approved too. Self-critique before handover, not after. (3) A VISIBLE CATALOG: eight rows of adjectives is not a choice anyone can make, so the catalog now draws 3-4 shortlisted systems on ONE canvas, same screen, same copy, same data — three different screens in three systems is a slideshow, not a comparison — carrying a dense region, an input in rest and error, a status signal and the app's real longest string in its real locale, which is where a Latin-first system stops looking neutral. That collided with design-canvas's own halt on recreating a look from memory, and the halt won: samples are CHARACTERIZATIONS drawn from each system's published values, labelled as such ON the artboard because a canvas outlives the conversation and gets forwarded without the handover, and adoption still runs through /clone-design, whose metric is fidelity measured from pixels. Where the published values cannot be read, draw fewer candidates rather than filling the gap from memory.
